info.title: Manifest
info.description: Manifest's public API (§22). Generated from the control plane's route definitions; do not edit. Resource routes are under /v1 (D23.8); a breaking change is a new prefix beside it. Response objects may gain fields under /v1 — a client ignores fields it does not know. Every mutation carries an Idempotency-Key, and a session-bearing mutation carries Origin (§20).

post.description: §22 step 5. Answers once the new instance serves, or once it has failed with an Incident — a failed deploy is a 200 whose state is `failed` (R3, §14). The previous instance keeps serving until the new one is proved, and drains in the background. Up to ~90 s when a release never becomes ready. Production answers 409 with LaunchReadiness (§13).

post.description: D24: lets the agent’s refused request through, ONCE. It grants that exact request — this token, this method, this path, this body — a single retry, which the agent makes itself; nothing is executed here on its behalf, and the retry is validated by its own route as any request is. Only a person who holds the capability themselves may confirm, and only in an interactive session.

get.description: Upgrade to a WebSocket. Builds, their log lines, instance state transitions, incidents and every other audit event for this project, as StreamFrames: the newest events first as a replay, then the ready frame, then live. A session-bearing upgrade must carry Origin (§20). A plain GET answers 426.

101.description: Switching Protocols. Every message is one StreamFrame, as JSON.

426.description: This endpoint is a WebSocket; a plain GET is answered EVENTS_UPGRADE_REQUIRED.

default.description: Refused before the upgrade, in the D23.7 envelope: UNAUTHENTICATED, NOT_FOUND (a stranger, or no such project), CSRF_ORIGIN_REFUSED, INTERNAL.

closeCodes.1001: The edge reloaded and its grace period ran out. Reconnect: the replay carries every event since.
closeCodes.1006: The upgrade was refused with an HTTP status — UNAUTHENTICATED, NOT_FOUND or CSRF_ORIGIN_REFUSED — or the connection dropped. A WebSocket client is shown no status; a plain GET of the same URL with the same session answers UNAUTHENTICATED or NOT_FOUND as the upgrade did (a GET is not origin-checked).
closeCodes.1011: The stream could not be opened; the operator log says why. Reconnect.
closeCodes.1013: The client fell behind (more than maxBufferedBytes queued). Reconnect to be replayed.
closeCodes.4403: The upgrade carried a session from another origin.

Approval.description: One decision about one release, kept for ever (§13).

reason.description: Required on a rejection: a refusal with no words is one nobody can act on (D23.7).

ApprovalDiff.description: The exact diff shown at decision time (§13).

path.description: Where, in manifest.yaml’s own vocabulary — the file an agent edits.

summary.description: The AI-written plain-English summary of what changed. **Null is a state, not an error** (Decision 7): an approval gate that fails closed on a language model being down is an outage, not a control. `summarySource` says why.

summarySource.description: `llm`: the model wrote it. `unavailable`: it could not be produced, and the diff beside it is the control. `no-previous-release`: this is a first launch, so there is nothing to diff.

review.description: R4 (D33, §15): the code reviewer’s verdict at decision time. `not_performed` until a reviewer is configured — an honest absence rather than a stub that purports to have reviewed.

burst.description: §24: do they all arrive at once.

Blueprint.description: A blueprint as a client chooses one: what it provides and the starters it offers. Never its base image or build internals.

starters.description: §25: what `POST /v1/projects` accepts as `starter` for this blueprint.

imageDigest.description: `sha256:…` once the build has succeeded; the image a release names.

error.description: Why a failed build failed, in words its author can act on (§14).

scan.description: Null until the build succeeds, and for a build from before scans were recorded.

ControlFrame.description: Ends the replay: everything after it is live.

slug.description: Checked by the same function as GET /v1/slugs/{slug} (§23).

starter.description: One the blueprint offers. Without one: the skeleton and a minimal manifest.

CreatedProject.description: §22 steps 2–3: the project, its environments, and the validation of the manifest its first commit carries.

slug.description: The project’s name, and the first label of every hostname it has (§23).

Fleet.description: §26’s fleet, administrators only. Not yet: department, custom domains, AI spend this month.

slugReserved.description: §23: holds a label reserved after it was created. Handle with the owner; never renamed automatically.

entityId.description: §9: fixed at registration and stored here rather than recomputed — which is also why a project slug is immutable after production launch.

certExpiresAt.description: D20: an unnoticed expiry silently kills login for a live course app.

registeredAttributes.description: WHAT UBC IAM ACTUALLY REGISTERED. A production build fails when a release asks for an attribute that is not in here (§7).

Incident.description: A failed deploy, as §14 records it: how it ended, what the platform checked, what the app printed, and what changed since it last worked.

logTail.description: The last 200 lines, redacted at capture (§14).

prompt.description: §14: shaped to be handed straight to an agent as a repair request.

Instance.description: A running (or once-running) copy of a release in one environment (§11). Never its driver or handle.

KnowledgePack.description: D25: the files that teach an agent to write a valid manifest.yaml and wire the blueprint, versioned with it.

LaunchReadiness.description: §13’s first-launch checklist, computed from what exists. A production deploy is refused with this exact value until every blocking item is met.

blocking.description: Whether this item gates production. `ready` is every BLOCKING item being met; a non-blocking item is shown and never refuses a launch (D33: `code-review`).

state.description: `unmet`: this item is tracked and is not satisfied — the reason says what to do. `not_built`: Manifest does not track it yet, and `builtBy` names what builds it — a plan, or for `code-review` a tracked hardening item.

LogFrame.description: One line of a build’s output, as it is written. Never replayed — GET /v1/builds/{buildId}/logs has them all.

ManifestErrorCode.description: A code inside `details`: §7 schema, §7 policy, or §25 blueprint compatibility.

Me.description: The person the session belongs to.

role.description: The platform role THIS SESSION is authorized as.

name.description: A person’s label for it, so a list of tokens is reviewable.

capabilities.description: The explicit set this token may use (D24). None of members:manage, release:promote, quota:set or secret:read: those are refused to a delegated token however it was minted.

expiresInDays.description: How long the token lives, in days. D24: a token has an expiry, and at most 365 days of one.

MintedToken.description: A newly minted delegated token, with its secret. The only time the secret exists.

secret.description: The token, in full: `mft_<id>_<secret>`. Shown ONCE. Store it now — the platform keeps only a hash and cannot show it again.

PendingAction.description: D24: a delegated token asked for one of the privileged four. A person confirms or rejects it; a confirmation grants that one request a single retry.

action.description: The privileged capability that was refused — one of D24’s four.

bodySha256.description: SHA-256 of the canonical request body, so a client can match its own.

summary.description: What was asked for, for the person who answers.

waitingSeconds.description: Seconds between the question being asked and it being answered — or, while it is still pending, now.

PendingActionList.description: The questions agents have put to the people who own this project, newest first (§26).

slug.description: The project’s name, and the first label of every hostname it has (§23).

starter.description: The starter the first commit was seeded from (§25); null for the skeleton alone.

registeredAttributes.description: Exactly the attributes UBC IAM registered, as the ticket lists them.

state.description: The state this record should now be in. It is reached along §9’s arrows from wherever it is — a first write into `active` is refused exactly as a later one is.

Rehearsal.description: A LOCAL, production-shaped rehearsal (D21 as P6a redefines it for a laptop): it proves the SHAPE of the registration and never UBC’s acceptance of it.

entityId.description: The entityID the Service Provider was registered under when this ran — read off the registration, never recomputed.

attributes.description: What the registration listed. Decision 10 compares these with what the candidate release would register now.

signInStatus.description: What the app answered at its registered ACS, or null when no assertion was produced.

attributesReleased.description: What the assertion ACTUALLY carried, as friendly names where the platform knows one. §9’s attribute release, measured rather than assumed.

RejectPendingActionRequest.description: A person’s refusal of a pending action, in their own words.

reason.description: Why this is refused. The agent is told, verbatim.

Release.description: Immutable: a build, a spec and the configuration resolved for every environment (§13).

scan.description: §12: its build’s scan, recorded on the Release.

sandbox.description: One environment’s view of the release, frozen when it was made (§13).

envNames.description: The names the app declares — never their values (P5a Decision 22).

staging.description: One environment’s view of the release, frozen when it was made (§13).

envNames.description: The names the app declares — never their values (P5a Decision 22).

production.description: One environment’s view of the release, frozen when it was made (§13).

envNames.description: The names the app declares — never their values (P5a Decision 22).

ScanSummary.description: §12’s scan of the image a build produced (§6 `Build.scan`).

scanner.description: The scanner and its version — `fake` from the in-memory driver.

databaseAgeDays.description: How old the vulnerability database was, in days; null when the scanner could not say, and then `stale` is true.

stale.description: A clean result from a stale database is not evidence there is nothing to find (§12).

baseImageKnown.description: False when the base image was not identified: every finding was attributed to the build, so `baseImage` counted nothing.

fixable.description: Introduced by this build, with a published fix. On a fresh database a build with any is refused (§12).

unfixable.description: Introduced by this build, with no published fix: recorded, not blocking (§12).

baseImage.description: The base image’s own — the blueprint’s to fix (§20).

unfixableFindings.description: The unfixable findings by id, at most 50; `unfixable` counts them all.

SlugCheck.description: §23: exactly what project creation will answer — advisory, since creation checks again.

reasons.description: Present when `available` is false: every reason that applies.

spec.description: manifest.yaml v1 as parsed and validated (§7). Its own JSON Schema is not published in P5a.

commitSha.description: A full commit id. Defaults to the commit of the newest validated spec.

StreamFrame.description: Every message on WS /v1/projects/{projectId}/events is one of these, as JSON. Switch on `kind`, then `type`.

Token.description: A delegated token (D24), scoped to one project and a capability set. Its secret is shown once, when it is minted, and is never readable again.

rateLimit.description: Requests a minute this token may make, enforced in the control plane (§20, P5b Task 9). Past it, every route answers 429 RATE_LIMITED with Retry-After.

expired.description: Whether this token is past its own expiresAt. Computed by the platform; a revoked token that has not expired is not expired.

x-manifest-unversioned.why: Browser-mediated sign-in. Its URL is part of the flow the Manifest IdP completes (§9), not a resource.

§20's step-up re-authentication (P6a Task 8). A browser navigation that ends at the IdP and returns through the ACS; it re-proves a person rather than naming a resource, and its answer is a redirect rather than a representation.
The ACS. Its URL is registered with the IdP in the platform's SP row (§9), so a prefix change would be an IdP registration change.
The console's own sign-out. Ends the browser's session; not a resource.

The SLO URL registered beside the ACS (§9), reached by the IdP's HTTP-Redirect binding, which is a GET. Declared POST-only until P5c sitting 9 found that single logout therefore 404'd against Manifest's own SP.
The registry token realm (§13). Its callers are the Docker daemon and BuildKit speaking the distribution token protocol, never a Manifest client.
The registry token realm, OAuth2 form grant. Same callers, same reason.
